1. `lem-green-type-i-boundary-identity`, proof step 1.2, and `lem-green-type-ii-boundary-identity`, proof step 1.2 — the cited Newton–Leibniz theorem does not cover a collapsed section.

   The region definition permits $\alpha=\beta$ or $\lambda=\rho$ at endpoints because strict separation is required only in the interior ([definition](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/def-type-i-type-ii-and-elementary-green-regions.md:30)). Nevertheless, both steps say they apply `[L4]` “for each” fixed coordinate ([Type I](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/lem-green-type-i-boundary-identity.md:54), [Type II](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/lem-green-type-ii-boundary-identity.md:54)). The cited theorem assumes strictly ordered endpoints: “Let $a<b$” ([dependency](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/thm-newton-leibniz-with-interior-derivative.md:30)).

   The identities remain true on a collapsed section because both sides are zero, so this is a sub-30-second degenerate-case gap, not a false conclusion.

   Severity: **nonfatal**.

2. `lem-green-boundary-cancellation-under-finite-gluing`, proof step 2.2 — boundedness is used before it is established.

   Step 2.2 invokes `[L5]` to conclude that the zero extensions are Riemann integrable ([item](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/lem-green-boundary-cancellation-under-finite-gluing.md:66)). The cited Lebesgue criterion begins, “A bounded real function…” ([dependency](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/thm-lebesgue-criterion-in-rn.md:35)). The proof establishes $|H|\le M$ from compactness only in the following step 3.1 ([item](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/lem-green-boundary-cancellation-under-finite-gluing.md:68)).

   The required fact follows immediately from the already-listed extreme-value fact `[L7]`, so this is a local ordering/citation gap. The subsequent bound $|q|\le NM1_S$ is correct.

   Severity: **nonfatal**.

3. `thm-path-independence-iff-zero-closed-loop-integrals`, proof step 1.2, and `thm-path-independent-field-has-a-potential-by-line-integrals`, steps 1.2–2.1 — arbitrary-domain paths are concatenated without normalization.

   Concatenation was defined only for paths $\alpha,\beta:[0,1]\to\mathbb R^n$ ([definition](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/def-piecewise-c1-path-operations-and-oriented-reparametrizations.md:28)). The equivalence proof takes arbitrary paths and immediately forms $\alpha*\beta^-$ ([item](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/thm-path-independence-iff-zero-closed-loop-integrals.md:49)); the potential proof similarly appends a $[0,1]$ coordinate segment to “any path” ([item](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/thm-path-independent-field-has-a-potential-by-line-integrals.md:50)).

   An orientation-preserving affine normalization to $[0,1]$ closes both arguments immediately, so this is nonfatal under the 30-second rule.

   Severity: **nonfatal**.
